title: Finn and the Hiccuping Dragon
markdown:
Once upon a time, in the warm and cozy Mossymoon Mountains, lived a little wizard called Finn. Finn loved magic! He loved making little spells go *fizz-pop* and *twinkle-shoo*. He made lights dance on his fingers. He made yellow flowers float like tiny balloons! And oh boy, Finn loved snacks! He loved munching on sunshine berries, which tasted like happy giggles. He loved cloud bread, which was softer than a bunny’s ear and tasted like sweet dreams. But sometimes, when Finn ate his yummy supper, he thought, "It would be even yummier with a friend!" He wished for someone to share his sunshine berries with. He imagined sharing a big sandwich made of cloud bread. He'd cut it in half. One half for him, and one half for his friend!

Every day, Finn would gather the juiciest sunshine berries, round and rosy and smelling like warm days. And he’d find the fluffiest cloud bread he could, so light it almost floated away! He’d spread his favorite checkered blanket, the one with squares of blue and yellow, on the softest, mossy path in the mountains. It was a lovely, peaceful path, winding between trees that looked like they had green fluff for leaves – they were called cloud-pines! Their branches drooped down like soft green curtains. The air smelled sweet, like flowers and moss! It felt warm and soft, like a hug. It was the perfect place for a quiet supper, a place where you could hear little rustles.

Until one day… SPLISH! SPLASH! Nope, not water. It was more of a tiny, *sniffle-snuffle*. Finn stopped spreading his blanket. He tilted his head. His wizard hat, the one that was a little too big and kept slipping over his bright, wondering eyes, nearly fell over them. *Sniffle-snuffle*. It was coming from behind a big, round, mossy stone that looked like a sleeping bear. Finn tiptoed closer, his wizard boots making soft *squish-squish* sounds on the springy ground. Each step felt like walking on a soft pillow.

And so, Finn peeked around the mossy stone, and guess what he saw? A little dragon! Not a big, roaring dragon, oh no! This dragon was about the size of a fluffy kitten, no bigger than Finn’s favorite cuddly toy. Its scales were green like emeralds, and they sparkled like little green stars in the soft light. Its wings looked like delicate dragonfly wings, all shimmery and see-through, fluttering just a little. The little dragon had big, round eyes that looked like bright pebbles, and a tiny nose that twitched when it thought. And it was definitely doing the sniffle-snuffle. Tears, like tiny, sparkly drops, were rolling down its cheeks.

Finn remembered his mama telling him to always be kind and to share smiles. So, he whispered, his voice as soft as a butterfly’s wing, "Hello there, little one. Are you alright? Why are you sniffing and snuffling?"

The dragon jumped a little, its sparkly wings giving a quick flutter, then it gave a tiny, wobbly smile. "Oh! Hello!" it squeaked, and tried to bow its head. It was very hard for a little dragon to bow properly, and its head wobbled a lot like a jelly on a plate. "My name is Flicker. I was hoping… could I watch you eat your supper? If that's okay?" Flicker looked down at his little dragon claws, a bit embarrassed.

Finn’s face lit up brighter than any spell he’d ever cast! A friend! For supper! "Watch? Oh, you don't have to just watch, Flicker! You can share my supper!" Finn chirped, already pulling out his yummy cloud bread. He carefully broke off a big piece.

And so, Finn sat down on his checkered blanket and offered Flicker a piece of cloud bread. Flicker took it very carefully with his dragon claws, making sure not to scratch the blanket. He nibbled it gently. He chewed and chewed, trying to be quiet and polite. Then, he ate a big, sweet sunshine berry. Oh! It was so juicy and delightful, bursting with sunny flavour! But Flicker was so excited about the berry, he let out a little, unexpected *HICCUP!* And with the hiccup came a tiny puff of smoke, like a little grey whisper that tickled Finn’s nose!

Finn didn't jump or get scared. He didn't even flinch! He just giggled! A big giggle that sounded like little bells. "Hee hee! That was a funny little puff! It tickled my nose!" he said. Flicker looked surprised, then a big smile spread across his little dragon face, and he giggled too, a little puff of smoke escaping with each giggle. "Oh dear," Flicker whispered, his nose twitching with amusement. "My mama said dragons shouldn't puff smoke when they eat. It's not right."

Finn patted the ground next to him, making space for Flicker. "It's okay! It just means you really, really liked the berry!" he said kindly. "It’s a yummy berry! Here, try another one! Maybe the juicy one!" He handed Flicker another big, sunshiny sunshine berry, glistening with sweet juice.

And so, Flicker and Finn munched happily on more sunshine berries and cloud bread. Flicker tried really hard not to hiccup smoke, but sometimes, a tiny little puff would escape when he was very happy, and Finn would just laugh. They talked about the sparkly spells Finn liked to make, and Flicker told Finn about how he loved to watch the butterflies flutter by, their wings like colorful silk. Finn found out that Flicker’s mama taught him to be polite by practicing saying "Thank you ever so much" and "May I please have another" to the wind.

Until finally, as the moonbeams started to twinkle through the cloud-pine leaves and make dancing patterns on Finn’s checkered blanket, they finished their supper. Flicker felt a little sleepy from all the yummy food and all the polite talking and giggling. He nudged Finn’s arm. Finn smiled a big, warm smile. He pet Flicker's green scales. They felt warm and smooth, like pretty stones. Flicker snuggled close to Finn, right on the soft moss. The air was still and quiet, filled with the gentle chirping of night crickets. It was the coziest, warmest feeling ever, like being wrapped in a soft blanket. The soft, mossy ground felt like a soft bed.

Ever since then, Finn and Flicker often shared suppers under the twinkling stars in the Mossymoon Mountains, with lots of sunshine berries that tasted like happiness, cloud bread that was softer than a dream, and happy giggles that sometimes, just sometimes, had a tiny puff of smoke attached. And Finn never ate supper alone again, because he had found his very best friend.
characters: Finn the young wizard, a little dragon
author: StoryGen Community
